Coal Preparation Facility Noise Level Contribution - The coal preparation facility located on Tract III would not be adequate for processing and shipping 26 million tons of coal proposed to be mined annually from both tracts under the high-level development scenario. Consequently, Tract II would require its own railroad spur and crushing and loading facilities. The proposed 3.5 mile railroad spur would connect the Tract II preparation facility to the existing Tract III railroad spur. Construction of this rail spur would make the haulage road from Tract II to Tract III unnecessary. The equivalent sound level contribution to nearby land uses from the construction of the railroad will be below existing ambient sound levels. The increase in ambient sound levels will be negligible.
For the anticipated level of development it is estimated that the equivalent sound level contribution at 1,000 feet from the center of the coal preparation facility is 52 dB, and for the high-level development, 50 dB and 52 dB are estimated for Tracts II and III, respectively (Dames & Moore, 1976).
Railroad Operations Noise Level Contribution - By 1989, when coal production is at its peak level under low-level development, it is estimated that there will be four train movements per day leaving the coal preparation facility. At full productivity under the high-level development (1992), approximately four trainloads per day would leave the Tract III facility and two trainloads per day would leave the Tract III facility.
